author: Jcarrill0
subject: [ROGUE] Lockpicking 1-300
content_md:
Please note that while this guide covers the best ways to power-level your lockpicking, it is perfectly feasible to level the vast majority of your skill simply by choosing to work quests that involve humanoids that can be pickpocketed for lockboxes, which can then be picked to raise your skill, and which also will sometimes contain Rogue poisons, thus increasing the value of this approach.

Early on you might get some Inv box 01 [[Practice Locks]](https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=6712) from an engineer to increase your lockpicking up to skill level 80. The quest to obtain Lockpicking will point you towards plenty of practice chests.

The best way for Alliance rogues to get their lockpicking skill up at level 16-20 (after getting the Pick Lock skill) is Alther's Mill in the Redridge Mountains region. The quest [20] Alther's Mill requires lockpicking a chest in Alther's Mill for a quest item and is close to the practice lockboxes. These chests respawn very quickly (you can stand between a couple or three and alternate between them) and may be practiced upon from 1 to over 100 skill. You do not have to be on the quest to pick these, so you can come back later to raise your skill when your level based skill cap is higher. If you do the quest at level 16, you should probably return at least once when you are over level 20. Horde rogues can similarly gain early levels from an equivalent quest on the ship off the Merchant Coast, south of Ratchet in the Barrens.
 *(Note: The above mentioned chest are not faction specific. If preferred Alliance characters could just as easily skillup lockpicking on chests found in the ship at the Merchant Coast. Vise-versa, it is possible for Horde characters to level on the chests found in Alther's Mill.)*

 **1-70** - The Barrens, Ship off of merchants coast. (Has yellow spikes in the front you can jump on to board)
Respawn timer 0.5 seconds. 10 Box spawn points.

 **1-70** - Redridge Mountains, Alther's Mill
Respawn timer 6 seconds. 5 Box spawn points.

 **70-120** - Redridge Mountains, Lake Everstill
Respawn timer 4 seconds. 7 Box spawn points.

 **70-120** - Westfall, Dustplains, Tower to the south
Respawn timer 0.1 second. 1 Box spawn point.

 **70-120** - The Barrens, Sledge Fen, Tower to northeast (apart of rogue poison profession quest)
Respawn timer 3-5 seconds. 1 Box spawn point.

 **110-150** - Wetlands, Murloc Camps (on land North of menethil harbor)
Respawn timer 10 seconds. 5 Box spawn points.

 **150-200** - Desolace, Sar'theris Strand:
Respawn timer precisely 3 minutes. 7 Box spawn points.
 *Note: By the time you make it back to the first one it will have respawned.*

 **200-250** - Searing Gorge, Slag Pit (Slave worker, non hostile area bottom area)
Respawn timer 9 seconds. 6 Box spawns points.

 **250-300** - Eastern PlagueLands, Tyr's Hand
Respawn timer 9 seconds. 4(definitely more) Box spawn points. 2 that avoid mobs in first area.

The rogue poisons quests for Horde and Alliance provide the next opportunity for solid skill gains. The quest can be picked up at level 20, although it may be too difficult for many players at level 20. The item required to complete this quest is contained inside a locked chest that can be picked repeatedly up to 170. (You are likely to hit your skill level cap first, if you are on the poison quest.) If you've already finished the quest, you can still use the chests to gain skill. The chests don't highlight when you mouse over them after the first time (when you obtain the quest item), so you have to activate your lockpicking skill first and then click the chest. The chest will be empty if you already have the quest item, or unpickable if you have completed the quest. Be sure to close the empty loot window in order to speed along the chest respawning (it is very quick if the loot window is not left open.) The poison Touch of Zanzil is applied every time the chest is lockpicked. The poisons can be dispelled if you have the cure from the poison quest chain, Anti-Venom skill (and Anti-Venom in your pack) from the First Aid profession, or by the dwarf racial Stoneform. It has also been confirmed that Jungle Remedy also cures this poison but requires the user to be level 22 or higher. The boss guarding the chest will probably respawn a couple of times while you are leveling your lockpicking skill on this chest. (It appears that either faction could use the opposite faction chest; not tested.)

Level 1 [Battered Footlockers](https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?search=Battered+Footlocker) can be pickpocketed from the mobs around Durnholde Keep in the Hillsbrad Foothills. Note again that these are level 1, so if you have already leveled up using the lockbox in the rogue poisons quest, these will be grey and therefore useless for leveling your skill. Inside Durnholde Keep there are footlockers scattered around the grounds that require a lockpicking skill of 100 to open which can help you level your skill.

At Bluegill Marsh in the Wetlands, there are Battered Footlockers with varying skill level requirement of 90, 100, and 110.

If you are level 30-40 you can go to Desolace, bring 2–3 hours worth of water breathing potions, and pick your way into the mid 200s. There are [Waterlogged Footlockers](https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?search=Waterlogged+Footlocker) around (37,21) off the northwest shore. There are level 33 mobs you will have to deal with while doing this. There are also Mossy Footlockers in the deeper areas that can get you to 225. These can be found in a NE running trench near the big island off the coast, around (36,11). Though they are few and far between here. A better place to find these is in the lake that surrounds the Sunken Temple in the Swamp of Sorrows.
Alternate Path.

If you don't like the water, you can head to Angor Fortress in the Badlands. There are two types of footlockers inside the fortress, Battered Footlockers and Dented Footlockers. The Battered Footlockers are located upstairs, and you will be able to open them immediately at 150; however, the Dented Footlockers will require a skill of 175 to open.

At 225, go to Searing Gorge. Down in the Slag Pit are [[Dented Footlockers]](https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?search=Dented+Footlocker). You can open all of them, and again pickpocket for junkboxes. Additionally, you can travel to the Swamp of Sorrows. A water-breathing potion makes circling the deep water around the Sunken Temple much easier, as [[Mossy Footlockers]](https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?search=Mossy+Footlocker) spawn throughout the area. Stay in either of these locations until 250-255.

The best place to raise your skill from 250 to 300 is in Blackrock Depths. Simply go in, turn to the left and unlock the Shadowforge Gate. Continue forward and take the first right, picking the next Shadowforge Gate. Pick the first door on the left, the East Garrison Door, and then head through the door, staying on the bottom level. If you are level 60 or above, pick the large wooden object sticking out of the ground below the giant gear, The Shadowforge Lock; lower levels can aggro the mobs around it. Pickpocket the 10 humanoid mobs in the room and you should average either 1 Sturdy Junkbox or 1 Heavy Junkbox each run. You can also lockpick cell doors if you are able to solo small groups before them. Then head out of the instance and reset it before doing all four again. *Note that you can only reset the instance 4 times before it disables you from entering, saying "You have entered too many instances recently".* This will yield 5 runs. This is valid for the whole account and resets roughly an hour after you entered the first time. Keep in mind that a number of mobs will be able to see through stealth, regardless of your level, so be prepared.

Another place for 250-300 is Tyr's Hand in Eastern Plaguelands. Pickpocket the mobs and find all of the [[Scarlet Footlockers]](https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?object=179498). In the time it takes to take a full circle of Tyr's Hand, the starting point will be pickpocketable and have boxes respawned. Do this until 300.

Another spot at Searing Gorge is the Stonewrought Pass. You can pick the doors on either side at around 225, however the Loch Modan side has an Alliance guard so Horde may find it easier to simply level on the Searing Gorge side. The door quickly closes after being opened, so you can continuously pick the door until it is grey.

author: Jadowsofel
subject: Demon Hunter build for Rogues
content_md:
Greetings all. *I am Jadowsofel/Shaldrazath, kaldorei/sindorei disciple of <Demon Hunter>.*

This guide will lay out a basic blueprint explaining how the build works along with some conjecture filtered through personal experience. It may or may not be the first of its' kind, but I've not seen such a build elsewhere before and am posting this now only because of the many inquiries and much interest that I've encountered since I began doing dungeons & raids recently. As a new build, the possibilities are still unknown and any notion of what could be considered optimal is speculation at best. Nonetheless, I offer this guide for those drawn to creative/off-meta modes of gameplay and hope that it will serve as a semblance of proof that some degree of innovation is still possible on this old game that we all love so much. **Please experiment for yourself.**

Two quick points before I begin:

 1) I'd like to mention & thank the user Portholes (player name Iag with a capital "i") for their post entitled "Elemental Cat Build". [viewtopic.php?t=6169](https://forum.turtlecraft.gg/viewtopic.php?t=6169) This was a catalyst of sorts which kindled the mechanical, nuts-and-bolts-level inspiration for much of this build.

 2) My calling this a demon hunter build merely reflects my own personal approach to the aesthetic & lore-derived interpretation for my gameplay. Essentially, this is a melee/magic, chaotic (proc-based) "*shadow warrior*" build.
/drink Mchealbolton/Doraexplora
As such, it can be interpreted in myriad ways depending on ones' own personal approach to aesthetics/fashion, idiosyncratic lore character background, etc. Please consider adjusting enchants and other non-essential items to best serve your own preferred manner of gameplay.  *However*. because the demon hunter was the original creative impetus that drove my efforts, I will continue to present this as a **Demon Hunter** build.

OK, so...

This is an exclusive TWoW **Rogue, Hunter and Warrior** build that, not unlike the Elemental Cat, primarily utilizes magic-damage-on-melee-hit effects to trigger the proc from the Blade of Eternal Darkness and/or
the Ornate Bloodstone Dagger. However, UNLIKE the Elemental Cat, the dual-wielding Rogue, Hunter and Warrior classes are privy to items and benefits that the Druid is not. I discovered that the weapon effect from the Blade of Eternal Darkness can be triggered by weapon enchants such as Fiery Weapon, Icy Chill and Lifestealing as well as from Shadow Oil and Dragonbreath Chili procs. Darkmoon Card: Maelstrom and Heart of Wyrmthalak can also proc the effect. Additionally, these classes can carry a bow which offers a magic-damage-on-melee-hit effect and also have access to Mail and Plate armor items that give the passive magic-damage-on-melee-hit effect as well.
Note: **The Blade of Eternal Darkness has no internal cooldown for its' weapon effect proc rate.**

See below for an example of an ideal gear setup:

 **Armor:**
Incendosaur Skin Gloves <https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=60582>
Incendosaur Skin Boots <https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=60568>
Incendosaur Skin Pauldrons <https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=60572>
Leggings of Fiery Temper <https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=61505>
Thunder Lizard's Hide <https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=81308> (Horde-only)
Ring of Electrical Binding <https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=61332>
Blazefury Medallion <https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=17111>
 **Weapons:**
Blade of Eternal Darkness <https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=17780>
Tempest's Rage <https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=83564>
Flamestring Bow <https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=80825>
 **Trinkets:**
Darkmoon Card: Maelstrom <https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=19289>
Heart of Wyrmthalak <https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=22321>
or
Hand of Justice <https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=11815>
 **Consumables:**
Dragonbreath Chili <https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=12217>
Shadow Oil <https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=3824>

Each item synergizes to maximize consistency rate of Blade of Eternal Darkness's (aka BoED's) weapon effect proc.
 **Note:** When considering your offhand weapon, I suggest focusing on weapon speed (the faster the better) and one that has an innate damage proc which may have it's own chance to proc the BoED's weapon effect.

Math has never been my forte but allow me to break this down as you consider the possibilities:
 **Blade of Eternal Darkness has a 10% chance to proc upon successful spell hit.**
 *Every successful melee strike you land will give you an additional **10** simultaneous spell hits from all of the passive magic-damage-on-melee-hit items.
 **This equates to a 65% proc rate for Blade of Eternal Darkness per successful melee strike.**
 *The 3-set bonus from the Incendosaur set grants an additional **5%** chance to land a magic attack upon successful melee strike which has it's own chance to proc the BoED weapon effect.
 *The Tempest's Rage has a **5-10%** chance to proc it's 15% haste ability. **More haste = more procs.**
 *Fiery/Icy/Lifestealing enchants have a proc rate that scales with weapon attack speed. At 1.5 this probably results in approximately a **5%** proc rate. Again, enchant procs can trigger BoED procs.
 *The Darkmoon:Maelstrom card and the Heart of Wyrmthalak both have approximately a **5%** proc rate and can themselves proc the BoED weapon effect.
 *Shadow Oil and Dragonbreath Chili both have a **5%** proc rate and can also proc the BoED.
Factoring this all together, the potential for immense burst damage becomes clear.

This brings me to my next point..

For a pure DPS(**Havoc**) variation, I propose (presuming that +hit is sufficient) that **haste is key.**
The concept is to land as many melee strikes in as quick a succession as possible so as to land as many procs as possible. This necessarily involves eschewing traditional defensive & offensive stats such as stamina, agility and strength so as to maximize melee strike output and thus **proc output.** The majority of your damage will come from magic damage via procs - not your melee weapons. Haste provides a static boost to your weapon attack speed and auto-attack continues concurrent to any queued special ability attack. **The global cooldown or GCD timer for abilities is 1.5 seconds**. This means that any haste increase will bring BoED below the GCD timer (+12% haste for Tempest's Rage) allowing for more auto-attacks to rotate on a separate, shorter timer within & during the cooldown of your primary ability attack of choice.

See below for a list of enchants/consumables/buffs that increase your haste:

 **Enchants:**
Enchant Gloves Minor Haste <https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?spell=13948>
 **Augmentations:**
Arcanum of Rapidity <https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=18329>
Sigil of Quickness <https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=61437>
 **Buffs:**
Warchief's Blessing [https://www.wowhead.com/classic/spell=1 ... s-blessing](https://www.wowhead.com/classic/spell=16609/warchiefs-blessing)
 **Consumables:**
Danonzo's Tel'Abim Medley <https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=60978#reward-of>
Potion of Quickness <https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=61181>
Juju Flurry <https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=12450>

There are of course many custom TWoW armor pieces that add haste as well. Mix these in wherever possible whilst ensuring that your +hit is sufficient.

Also consider that rogues have the innate means of increasing haste via abilities such as Slice and Dice, Blade Flurry 1/1, Sword Specialization 5/5 and Adrenaline Rush 1/1.
Rogue's also have Thistle Tea for more energy. More energy = more ability attacks = more procs.

 **As a rogue**, this build also potentially allows for **tanking** variation where you focus on **stamina**, **agility** and/or **armor** instead of haste. This is because rapid procs can generate rapid threat. Combined with the rogue's unique **Agitating Poison** (<https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=65032>) available here on TWoW and many defensive abilities such as Evasion, Ghostly Strikes, etc., it's certainly a variation to consider.
Indeed, **Vengeance** is one of the two talent specs of the demon hunter.

Now to my final point..

Another dimension to this build is the fact that both Shadow Oil (56%) and Dragonbreath Chili (100%) scale with spell power. This allows for the build to somewhat prioritize the inclusion of +spell power into the setup. Though the grind to exalted with Cenarion Circle is daunting to say the least, keep in mind that the nature of this build will allow for **perpetual uptime for the Wrath of Cenarius item proc**, further increasing the damage of the Oil & Chili. Thus, I consider this to be the other of the two BiS rings for this build.

Here's a list of some items to increase spell damage synergy:

 **Armor:**
Wrath of Cenarius <https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=21190>
 **Consumables:**
Dreamtonic <https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=61423>
Greater Arcane Elixir <https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=13454>
Flask of Supreme Spellpower <https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=13512>
Gilneas Hot Stew <https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=84041>
Gift of Arthas <https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=9088>

 **Doubtless there will be items and consumables, some finite, that I've missed but the information and lists above will at least provide a reasonably attainable basis for players to strive for that can bring this build to life.**

Here I offer an approach to talents for both pure DPS (**Havoc**) and tanking (**Vengeance**). As stated several times already, I implore you to **experiment** and **create** a style that best suits **your own** manner of gameplay.
This is only a suggestion:

 **Havoc:** <https://talents.turtlecraft.gg/rogue/0XF6-2UZ10Z1UC6>
 **Vengeance:** <https://talents.turtlecraft.gg/rogue/2RF60U-2UZD021UC6>
or perhaps [https://talents.turtlecraft.gg/rogue/2I ... 21UC6-UE66](https://talents.turtlecraft.gg/rogue/2IE-2UZD021UC6-UE66)

I'm happy & proud to share this guide with the server and hope that it might **inspire** you to try it yourself and even consider playing this build as a glaive-wielding kalorei or sin'dorei demon hunter too, or, better yet, **inspire** you to **innovate** a **new** build or approach to gameplay of **your own**.

 */bow*

Blazefury Medallion https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=17111
Weapons:
Blade of Eternal Darkness https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=17780
Tempest's Rage https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=83564
Flamestring Bow https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=80825
Trinkets:
Darkmoon Card: Maelstrom https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=19289
Heart of Wyrmthalak https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=22321
or
Hand of Justice https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=11815
Consumables:
Dragonbreath Chili https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=12217
Shadow Oil https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=3824

Each item synergizes to maximize consistency rate of Blade of Eternal Darkness's (aka BoED's) weapon effect proc.
Note: When considering your offhand weapon, I suggest focusing on weapon speed (the faster the better) and one that has an innate damage proc which may have it's own chance to proc the BoED's weapon effect.

Math has never been my forte but allow me to break this down as you consider the possibilities:
Blade of Eternal Darkness has a 10% chance to proc upon successful spell hit.
*Every successful melee strike you land will give you an additional 10 simultaneous spell hits from all of the passive magic-damage-on-melee-hit items.
This equates to a 65% proc rate for Blade of Eternal Darkness per successful melee strike.
*The 3-set bonus from the Incendosaur set grants an additional 5% chance to land a magic attack upon successful melee strike which has it's own chance to proc the BoED weapon effect.
*The Tempest's Rage has a 5-10% chance to proc it's 15% haste ability. More haste = more procs.
*Fiery/Icy/Lifestealing enchants have a proc rate that scales with weapon attack speed. At 1.5 this probably results in approximately a 5% proc rate. Again, enchant procs can trigger BoED procs.
*The Darkmoon:Maelstrom card and the Heart of Wyrmthalak both have approximately a 5% proc rate and can themselves proc the BoED weapon effect.
*Shadow Oil and Dragonbreath Chili both have a 5% proc rate and can also proc the BoED.
Factoring this all together, the potential for immense burst damage becomes clear.

This brings me to my next point..

For a pure DPS(Havoc) variation, I propose (presuming that +hit is sufficient) that haste is key.
The concept is to land as many melee strikes in as quick a succession as possible so as to land as many procs as possible. This necessarily involves eschewing traditional defensive & offensive stats such as stamina, agility and strength so as to maximize melee strike output and thus proc output. The majority of your damage will come from magic damage via procs - not your melee weapons. Haste provides a static boost to your weapon attack speed and auto-attack continues concurrent to any queued special ability attack. The global cooldown or GCD timer for abilities is 1.5 seconds. This means that any haste increase will bring BoED below the GCD timer (+12% haste for Tempest's Rage) allowing for more auto-attacks to rotate on a separate, shorter timer within & during the cooldown of your primary ability attack of choice.

See below for a list of enchants/consumables/buffs that increase your haste:

Enchants:
Enchant Gloves Minor Haste https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?spell=13948
Augmentations:
Arcanum of Rapidity https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=18329
Sigil of Quickness https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=61437
Buffs:
Warchief's Blessing https://www.wowhead.com/classic/spell=1 ... s-blessing
Consumables:
Danonzo's Tel'Abim Medley https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=60978#reward-of
Potion of Quickness https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=61181
Juju Flurry https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=12450

There are of course many custom TWoW armor pieces that add haste as well. Mix these in wherever possible whilst ensuring that your +hit is sufficient.

Also consider that rogues have the innate means of increasing haste via abilities such as Slice and Dice, Blade Flurry 1/1, Sword Specialization 5/5 and Adrenaline Rush 1/1.
Rogue's also have Thistle Tea for more energy. More energy = more ability attacks = more procs.

As a rogue, this build also potentially allows for tanking variation where you focus on stamina, agility and/or armor instead of haste. This is because rapid procs can generate rapid threat. Combined with the rogue's unique Agitating Poison (https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=65032) available here on TWoW and many defensive abilities such as Evasion, Ghostly Strikes, etc., it's certainly a variation to consider.
Indeed, Vengeance is one of the two talent specs of the demon hunter.

Now to my final point..

Another dimension to this build is the fact that both Shadow Oil (56%) and Dragonbreath Chili (100%) scale with spell power. This allows for the build to somewhat prioritize the inclusion of +spell power into the setup. Though the grind to exalted with Cenarion Circle is daunting to say the least, keep in mind that the nature of this build will allow for perpetual uptime for the Wrath of Cenarius item proc, further increasing the damage of the Oil & Chili. Thus, I consider this to be the other of the two BiS rings for this build.

Here's a list of some items to increase spell damage synergy:

Armor:
Wrath of Cenarius https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=21190
Consumables:
Dreamtonic https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=61423
Greater Arcane Elixir https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=13454
Flask of Supreme Spellpower https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=13512
Gilneas Hot Stew https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=84041
Gift of Arthas https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=9088

Doubtless there will be items and consumables, some finite, that I've missed but the information and lists above will at least provide a reasonably attainable basis for players to strive for that can bring this build to life.

Here I offer an approach to talents for both pure DPS (Havoc) and tanking (Vengeance). As stated several times already, I implore you to experiment and create a style that best suits your own manner of gameplay.
This is only a suggestion:

Havoc: https://talents.turtlecraft.gg/rogue/0XF6-2UZ10Z1UC6
Vengeance: https://talents.turtlecraft.gg/rogue/2RF60U-2UZD021UC6
or perhaps https://talents.turtlecraft.gg/rogue/2I ... 21UC6-UE66

I'm happy & proud to share this guide with the server and hope that it might inspire you to try it yourself and even consider playing this build as a glaive-wielding kalorei or sin'dorei demon hunter too, or, better yet, inspire you to innovate a new build or approach to gameplay of your own.

/bow

author: Bigsmerf
subject: Fixing Rogues
content_md:
I'd like to preface this with the fact that I do not play rogue, and I haven't studied the class much beyond other "Rogue bad waahhh" posts and all I know is that they're underperforming and why that is. No we're not talkin' about PvP here. I'd just like to bring more attention to the PvE side of things and help y'all get the publicity you need there. Here's the deal.

Combat and Assass are more or less pure DPS specs with practically zero utility. What special things they do have can be done by other classes. Warriors and shamans have low risk interrupts to replace kick, mages have polymorphs and warlocks have banishes to replace sap, sunder armor, fearie fire and certain weapons trump expose armor, you get the idea. What's rogue's counter?

A support tree that requires you dump all your talent points into it to fill the lack of support tools. This same spec deals the same amount of damage as tanks. Did I mention you have to spec into it?

You get the idea. Even when the devs try to deviate and make rogue fill a different niche it loses out on so much trying to do that. The solution(s)?

Make assass and combat do better ST damage. AOE is not necessary if they can fill the niche of being top performers in single target centric fights, which is pretty much all of them in raiding. Putting rogue in the upper echelon of this niche will give them, well- a niche... Which they need. Badly.

Bake some damage stuff into subtlety talents to make it so you're not poking at patchwerk with destructive power comparable to a gnome in pillowy battle armor wearing squeaky toy brass knuckles.

Thanks for coming to my TED talk. 5000 hours baby.

author: Akos1896
subject: Re: Fixing Rogues
content_md:
I give my 2 cents too about this.
Rogues have many special 'quirks' but they translate badly to raiding:
 * stealth and stuns don't really help
 * venom is a weird sharpening stone at OH (MH is supposed to have WF)
 * small gimmicks like trap disarm, misdirection or expose armor help but they are not consistently good enough to be called a utility kit
 * at the end of the day combat rogues are single-target fury warriors who refuse to tank

How I'd change it:
Combat and subtlety are easy. All combat needs is a number tweak with some extra caution. PVP still exists in this server, you have to figure out how to raise combat's damage profile without making a cancer in PVP. Note, they should be at least on par with fury warriors who among otherscan spam execute at low enemy health.
Overall raise of rogue DPS might be too toxic for PVP, giving a kind of execute to rogues might be toxic, too. They need an increase in the damage profile but this increase has to be done very cleverly.
Subtlety is easy too, since we know what TWOW Team wants to achieve.
But.
Reagents are for rare and situational abilities. I refuse to believe that a standard rotation should force you to use reagents.
Damage is also way too bad. Hybrids show us that in this server having utility doesn't have a big tax. Sub should perform below combat but should way outdo tanks.

Assassination is the interesting tree. Rogues go there to buy some talents but I refuse to believe that assassination builds, mostly relying on this tree actually exist. Maybe some theorycrafters here and there but that's all.
In my eyes, assassination is the only remaining tree in the server which doesn't provide a clear picture of what it does. Sure, you get some crit and venom synergies, cool. But I've yet to see assassination rogues in raid, read about assassination-specific rotation etc.
They need an identity first.
I'd go the middle way and make them a half-utility tree. More damage than subs. Utility coming from unique venom types - some could be equally impactful as a warlock curse, making raids happy if they have 1-2 assassination rogues.

subject: Re: Assa changes good, but we need guns!
content_md:
> **Kerenis wrote: Sun Aug 24, 2025 9:21 am**
> Noxious Assault does more damage with slow weapons thoug

Not true. It doesn't use weapon damage values at all. It's a % of your total attack power. If your attack power is the same with two slow 2.5+ speed weapons as it is with two fast 1.5 speed weapons, it will hit the same damage. Attack power normalization does not apply to spells that do not use weapon damage in the formula.

Which means that fast weapons are actually optimal for assassination because the weapon speed doesn't matter for noxious assault, but it DOES matter for how frequently you can apply poisons through auto attacks. More swings = more procs = more damage.

And assa is like 50%+ poison damage.

If i see anything else about the Assassination spec I will add it here and if someone has a question? I might be able to answer, might not but I think I got the rotation down, we'll see.

I'm torn between enchants,

Crusader = 100 strength for 15 sec x 2 (ya I know there is a heal too, blah)
Agility = 15 agility x2

I think that Agility would have better synergy with assassination due to the Seal Fate talent and raid buffs. more crit. more combo points and just over all everything criting more + the 30 attack power, which would be more with buffs. (can I get a Kings buff plz)

where crusader does have the chance to raise attack power by 100 or 200 if double proc which would raise the damage of auto attacks, Noxious Assaults and Eviscerate.

If I remember correctly Crusader has a lower procs per minute on faster weapons, Hmmmm? I'll have to look into that

I'm leaning towards agility, what do you all think?

Rotation:

My rotation as it is so far (this will be a mess and I'm only talking for myself)
How I maintain keeping up 2 finishers and weaving in Eviscerates or Rupture

I'm not worried about which opener I use. I want a combo point, period.

Depending on the mob will affect which opener, you wont garrote a stone elemental for example.

I want a combo point and from my experience I just need one to start my rotation.

I use my opener and I get a combo point, I hit envenom to get the poison buff going and since it is a finishing move it has 100% of the time so far, granted me another combo point, I hit slice and dice.

Now I have slice and dice and envenom up, but the problem is they both run out about the same time. I have 12 seconds before both expire. Because I used 1 combo point for each.

I have to get a 10-12 second separation between these 2 finishers to keep them up,
Without the RNG Gods stepping in via the Seal Fate Talent, or an energy boost from  [Stormshroud Set](https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?itemset=142%5B/url)  it looks something like this.

it takes using Noxious Assault 10-12 seconds to acquire 5 combo points.

I have 5 combo points and about 1-2 seconds before Slice and dice and Envenom expire.
I use my 5 combo points on Envenom which resets the timer to 28 seconds and since it is a finishing move I will automatically get a combo point, which I use to refresh slice and dice to 13 seconds.

I now have the separation I want, the next 5 combo points as you can probably guess will go to slice and dice, refreshing it to 30 seconds and I start looking at the time left on Envenom, it just flip flop back and forth like that.

Regardless if it's Slice and dice or Envenom you need to mentally make sure you are working on getting the 5 combo points starting at the 10-12 second and by the time the timer gets down to 1-2 seconds left you should have your 5 combo points.

The RNG Gods and you:
Because of the Talents we choose,  we can have combo points just dropping out of thin air.
[Stormshroud Set](https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?itemset=142%5B/url) has a chance to restore 30 energy and increase you attack speed by 10% for 8 seconds. In that 8 second window you swinging faster which feeds into the Vigor talent. Higher poison application, higher energy recovery in that 8 second window.

It's the RNG gods that are going to give you your Eviscerates or Ruptues, you can use a 3-5 combo point Eviscerate or Rupture as long as you stick to the rule of keeping separation between slice and dice and envenom. THEY HAVE TO STAY UP.
Rotation mistakes happen, just get back in your game and start over at the beginning.

Pool your energy and don't mash buttons. You will gain more dps having patience. Don't rush the rotation but let it flow.

In the rotation the damage might seem slow at the start but as mention by someone else in this tread over 50% of you damage will be poisons .
 25-27% will be auto hits
Noxious Assault 15-17%
Eviscerate 6-7%
will be slightly different due to gear differences. this is just a ball park figure I got from testing this rotation on the training dummy.

If your looking to pad your damage at the beginning of the fight, use an on use trinket you can also use [Oil of Immolation](https://www.wowhead.com/classic/item=8956/oil-of-immolation%5B/url) I know it's only a lvl 31 item but it does an extra 250 damage over 15 seconds, instant cast and has no cool down. it's spam-able every 15 seconds and the 250 damage is for each mob in a 3 yard radius, which is a benefit to our lack luster aoe.

[Dragonbreath chili](https://www.wowhead.com/classic/item=12217/dragonbreath-chili%5B/url) has a chance to do fire damage in a cone in front of the caster doing 60 damage to each mob.

Just a couple I know of and I realize some of you are more geared than I am and probably doing end game so a lot of this stuff is for new and up coming rogues

 **Poisons**

Assassination goes through a lot of poisons. I should explain. ( Hold on to your hat Dorothy, Kansas is going bye bye).

JMHO

(Sigh) Because of the 1.3 speed daggers, now lower that dagger speed to 1.25,  .97 or .87, common sense would be you are applying poisons even faster. (ie. auto attacks and combo point builder)

We have Talents that affect poison application:
Improved Poisons Increases the chance to apply poisons by 10%
Envenom Improves the chance to apply poisons to you target by 30%
Noxious Assault Strike with both weapons and applies poisons from both weapons
Slice and Dice Faster you swing the faster you chew through your poisons

now let's look at synergy between 2 other talents

Vigor Each time you poison your target you have a 100% chance to add 2 energy
Seal Fate Critical strikes from abilities that add combo points have a 100% chance to add an additional combo point.
The faster the Dagger, the higher the chance of poison application = the faster the return of energy returned to you.
That faster return of energy will be funneled into Noxious Assault Which in turn causes 2 poison stacks to disappear and gives you 1-2 combo points.
Combo points are collected to use 85% of the time on these 2 Finishers. Both feed into poison depletion
Slice and Dice
Envenom

It is a snake eating it's own tail. It's diabolical
The whole circular process is just chewing through poison stacks

but Shananagas? Isn't there something to help assassination rogue negate poison depletion?
There is a talent:
Efficient Poisons: Gives your poison application a 45% chance not to consume a charge. (A CHANCE!)
I must be the most unluckiest rogue on the planet!

With poisons falling off so fast
Assassination rogues that go OOP (out of Poisons) are just knee high gnomes tickling the boss's ankle with a feather

What I submitted due to the poison problem.

I agree
I'm an assassination rogue and the depletion of poisons is way to fast.

Efficient Poison talent is only a 45% Chance not to consume a charge. (A Chance?)

using 1.3 daggers and you throw in slice and dice and if you are wearing the [Stormshroud Armor](https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?itemset=142%5B/url)
and the 4 set procs my dagger speed is .87

I have had to revert to keeping an extra set of daggers in my bags and making a weapon swap macro
so that during trash or boss fights I can switch out because of the randomness of the 45% chance not to
consume poison charges.
Not to mention now having to double up poison purchases and loosing 2 more bag spaces.

How would I fix it?

I would just switch the talents Noxious Assault and Envenom
making Envenom the cap stone talent.

Envenom would then increase the effectiveness and chance to apply poison by 30% and also not consume your
poisons but make them 1 hour duration.

Then change Efficient Poison talent: by just taking out the bit of consuming a poison charge, and keeping the reduced chance to resist.

Envenom is a finishing move, why it's not the cap stone is beyond me.

BOOM! I have just now fixed Assassination rogue.

I am melting my enemies

Now I have slice and dice and envenom up, but the problem is they both run out about the same time. I have 12 seconds before both expire. Because I used 1 combo point for each.

I have to get a 10-12 second separation between these 2 finishers to keep them up,
Without the RNG Gods stepping in via the Seal Fate Talent, or an energy boost from Stormshroud Set it looks something like this.

it takes using Noxious Assault 10-12 seconds to acquire 5 combo points.

I have 5 combo points and about 1-2 seconds before Slice and dice and Envenom expire.
I use my 5 combo points on Envenom which resets the timer to 28 seconds and since it is a finishing move I will automatically get a combo point, which I use to refresh slice and dice to 13 seconds.

I now have the separation I want, the next 5 combo points as you can probably guess will go to slice and dice, refreshing it to 30 seconds and I start looking at the time left on Envenom, it just flip flop back and forth like that.

Regardless if it's Slice and dice or Envenom you need to mentally make sure you are working on getting the 5 combo points starting at the 10-12 second and by the time the timer gets down to 1-2 seconds left you should have your 5 combo points.

The RNG Gods and you:
Because of the Talents we choose, we can have combo points just dropping out of thin air.
Stormshroud Set has a chance to restore 30 energy and increase you attack speed by 10% for 8 seconds. In that 8 second window you swinging faster which feeds into the Vigor talent. Higher poison application, higher energy recovery in that 8 second window.

It's the RNG gods that are going to give you your Eviscerates or Ruptues, you can use a 3-5 combo point Eviscerate or Rupture as long as you stick to the rule of keeping separation between slice and dice and envenom. THEY HAVE TO STAY UP.
Rotation mistakes happen, just get back in your game and start over at the beginning.

Pool your energy and don't mash buttons. You will gain more dps having patience. Don't rush the rotation but let it flow.

In the rotation the damage might seem slow at the start but as mention by someone else in this tread over 50% of you damage will be poisons .
25-27% will be auto hits
Noxious Assault 15-17%
Eviscerate 6-7%
will be slightly different due to gear differences. this is just a ball park figure I got from testing this rotation on the training dummy.

If your looking to pad your damage at the beginning of the fight, use an on use trinket you can also use Oil of Immolation I know it's only a lvl 31 item but it does an extra 250 damage over 15 seconds, instant cast and has no cool down. it's spam-able every 15 seconds and the 250 damage is for each mob in a 3 yard radius, which is a benefit to our lack luster aoe.

Dragonbreath chili has a chance to do fire damage in a cone in front of the caster doing 60 damage to each mob.

Just a couple I know of and I realize some of you are more geared than I am and probably doing end game so a lot of this stuff is for new and up coming rogues

Poisons

Assassination goes through a lot of poisons. I should explain. ( Hold on to your hat Dorothy, Kansas is going bye bye).

JMHO

(Sigh) Because of the 1.3 speed daggers, now lower that dagger speed to 1.25, .97 or .87, common sense would be you are applying poisons even faster. (ie. auto attacks and combo point builder)

We have Talents that affect poison application:
Improved Poisons Increases the chance to apply poisons by 10%
Envenom Improves the chance to apply poisons to you target by 30%
Noxious Assault Strike with both weapons and applies poisons from both weapons
Slice and Dice Faster you swing the faster you chew through your poisons

now let's look at synergy between 2 other talents

Vigor Each time you poison your target you have a 100% chance to add 2 energy
Seal Fate Critical strikes from abilities that add combo points have a 100% chance to add an additional combo point.
The faster the Dagger, the higher the chance of poison application = the faster the return of energy returned to you.
That faster return of energy will be funneled into Noxious Assault Which in turn causes 2 poison stacks to disappear and gives you 1-2 combo points.
Combo points are collected to use 85% of the time on these 2 Finishers. Both feed into poison depletion
Slice and Dice
Envenom

It is a snake eating it's own tail. It's diabolical
The whole circular process is just chewing through poison stacks

but Shananagas? Isn't there something to help assassination rogue negate poison depletion?
There is a talent:
Efficient Poisons: Gives your poison application a 45% chance not to consume a charge. (A CHANCE!)
I must be the most unluckiest rogue on the planet!

With poisons falling off so fast
Assassination rogues that go OOP (out of Poisons) are just knee high gnomes tickling the boss's ankle with a feather


What I submitted due to the poison problem.

I agree
I'm an assassination rogue and the depletion of poisons is way to fast.

Efficient Poison talent is only a 45% Chance not to consume a charge. (A Chance?)

using 1.3 daggers and you throw in slice and dice and if you are wearing the Stormshroud Armor
and the 4 set procs my dagger speed is .87

I have had to revert to keeping an extra set of daggers in my bags and making a weapon swap macro
so that during trash or boss fights I can switch out because of the randomness of the 45% chance not to
consume poison charges.
Not to mention now having to double up poison purchases and loosing 2 more bag spaces.

How would I fix it?

I would just switch the talents Noxious Assault and Envenom
making Envenom the cap stone talent.

Envenom would then increase the effectiveness and chance to apply poison by 30% and also not consume your
poisons but make them 1 hour duration.

Then change Efficient Poison talent: by just taking out the bit of consuming a poison charge, and keeping the reduced chance to resist.

Envenom is a finishing move, why it's not the cap stone is beyond me.

BOOM! I have just now fixed Assassination rogue.









I am melting my enemies

Dragonbreath chili has a chance to do fire damage in a cone in front of the caster doing 60 damage to each mob.

Just a couple I know of and I realize some of you are more geared than I am and probably doing end game so a lot of this stuff is for new and up coming rogues

Poisons

Assassination goes through a lot of poisons. I should explain. ( Hold on to your hat Dorothy, Kansas is going bye bye).

JMHO

(Sigh) Because of the 1.3 speed daggers, now lower that dagger speed to 1.25, .97 or .87, common sense would be you are applying poisons even faster. (ie. auto attacks and combo point builder)

We have Talents that affect poison application:
Improved Poisons Increases the chance to apply poisons by 10%
Envenom Improves the chance to apply poisons to you target by 30%
Noxious Assault Strike with both weapons and applies poisons from both weapons
Slice and Dice Faster you swing the faster you chew through your poisons

now let's look at synergy between 2 other talents

Vigor Each time you poison your target you have a 100% chance to add 2 energy
Seal Fate Critical strikes from abilities that add combo points have a 100% chance to add an additional combo point.
The faster the Dagger, the higher the chance of poison application = the faster the return of energy returned to you.
That faster return of energy will be funneled into Noxious Assault Which in turn causes 2 poison stacks to disappear and gives you 1-2 combo points.
Combo points are collected to use 85% of the time on these 2 Finishers. Both feed into poison depletion
Slice and Dice
Envenom

It is a snake eating it's own tail. It's diabolical
The whole circular process is just chewing through poison stacks

but Shananagas? Isn't there something to help assassination rogue negate poison depletion?
There is a talent:
Efficient Poisons: Gives your poison application a 45% chance not to consume a charge. (A CHANCE!)
I must be the most unluckiest rogue on the planet!

With poisons falling off so fast
Assassination rogues that go OOP (out of Poisons) are just knee high gnomes tickling the boss's ankle with a feather


What I submitted due to the poison problem.

I agree
I'm an assassination rogue and the depletion of poisons is way to fast.

Efficient Poison talent is only a 45% Chance not to consume a charge. (A Chance?)

using 1.3 daggers and you throw in slice and dice and if you are wearing the Stormshroud Armor
and the 4 set procs my dagger speed is .87

I have had to revert to keeping an extra set of daggers in my bags and making a weapon swap macro
so that during trash or boss fights I can switch out because of the randomness of the 45% chance not to
consume poison charges.
Not to mention now having to double up poison purchases and loosing 2 more bag spaces.

How would I fix it?

I would just switch the talents Noxious Assault and Envenom
making Envenom the cap stone talent.

Envenom would then increase the effectiveness and chance to apply poison by 30% and also not consume your
poisons but make them 1 hour duration.

Then change Efficient Poison talent: by just taking out the bit of consuming a poison charge, and keeping the reduced chance to resist.

Envenom is a finishing move, why it's not the cap stone is beyond me.

BOOM! I have just now fixed Assassination rogue.









I am melting my enemies

Equiped level of 42
 1. A one hand Axe
 2. 1.50 speed (nice)
 3. DPS 35.3
 4. damage range of 37-69
 5 Chance on hit: Grants 1 extra attack on your next swing
Oh and it's PURPLE! Oh, How the monkeys have been train to luv the color purple. lol I admit I am a butt scratching monkey too. :)

For a level 42 it's awesome. I don't have the deep pockets to buy 2 of them but someone might and the question is at what point will you replace them with daggers. :) (Because you're going to   insidious_turtle  )

Let's talk weapon skill and chance for an extra attack on your next swing.

Weapon skill: The weapon skill is capped at 315
The higher the skill the more you push misses and glancing blows off the hit table, in effect landing more attacks
which means more poison procs that turns into energy return.
Also less glancing blows = more hits that have a chance to be crits and those crits can turn into more combo points.

(A CHANCE) on hit to get an extra attack:
The  [Flurry Axe](https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=871%5B/url) has a 1.5 - 2% chance to proc an extra attack, now some have said they FEEL like the proc chance is closer to 4-5% IDK but imho there is nowhere that states the extra attack proc will land 100% of the time, so the extra attack does have a chance to MISS.

You can get weapon skill for Axes, it's just so much easier to get for Daggers.

for Axes you can get [Goldminers Helmet](https://www.wowhead.com/classic/item=9375/expert-goldminers-helmet%5B/url) A level 33 Helm with Agi and Stam +7 to Axes ( Damn good for a level 33)

and there could be more gear out there for + axes that I'm not aware of.
As your gear progresses and ( I don't know what level you are) as you level, fast Daggers will just out preform axes, swords and maces (Hock,Spit)

[Alcor's Sunrazor](https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=14555%5B/url) vs. [Flurry Axe](https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=871%5B/url) Main hand.
[Distracting Dagger](https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=18392%5B/url) vs. [Flurry Axe](https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=871%5B/url) Off hand

It's to bad that Dwarves don't have an Axe racial like Humans have for Swords and Maces.
Duel wielding axes would be cool to see on a dwarf

Bottom line (jmho)

If you're level 42 and gots a boat load of gold (Hey Daddy, I'll be your Femboy) to buy 2  [Flurry Axes](https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=871%5B/url) Go for it, but by the time you get to your mid level 50's you will most likely be wanting to replace them IF you are planning on end content raiding.

I searched the [Axe Data Base](https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?items=2.0#0+5+1%5B/url) and it is the fastest axe in game and axes get slower quickly as the level goes up.

as I write this (10-13-20025) 1 Flurry axe is selling on Server Nordanaar for 400g, to duel wield, 800g
At this time only 1 is for sale

with just 400g you can buy the entire [Stromshoud Armor Set](https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?itemset=142%5B/url) (Highly recommend)

Choose your own path and have fun, at the end of the day that's what it's all about.

My rotation as it is so far (this will be a mess and I'm only talking for myself)
How I maintain keeping up 2 finishers and weaving in Eviscerates or Rupture

I'm not worried about which opener I use. I want a combo point, period.

Depending on the mob will affect which opener, you wont garrote a stone elemental for example.

I want a combo point and from my experience I just need one to start my rotation.

I use my opener and I get a combo point, I hit envenom to get the poison buff going and since it is a finishing move it has 100% of the time so far, granted me another combo point, I hit slice and dice.

Now I have slice and dice and envenom up, but the problem is they both run out about the same time. I have 12 seconds before both expire. Because I used 1 combo point for each.

I have to get a 10-12 second separation between these 2 finishers to keep them up,
Without the RNG Gods stepping in via the Seal Fate Talent, or an energy boost from Stormshroud Set it looks something like this.

it takes using Noxious Assault 10-12 seconds to acquire 5 combo points.

I have 5 combo points and about 1-2 seconds before Slice and dice and Envenom expire.
I use my 5 combo points on Envenom which resets the timer to 28 seconds and since it is a finishing move I will automatically get a combo point, which I use to refresh slice and dice to 13 seconds.

I now have the separation I want, the next 5 combo points as you can probably guess will go to slice and dice, refreshing it to 30 seconds and I start looking at the time left on Envenom, it just flip flop back and forth like that.

Regardless if it's Slice and dice or Envenom you need to mentally make sure you are working on getting the 5 combo points starting at the 10-12 second and by the time the timer gets down to 1-2 seconds left you should have your 5 combo points.

The RNG Gods and you:
Because of the Talents we choose, we can have combo points just dropping out of thin air.
Stormshroud Set has a chance to restore 30 energy and increase you attack speed by 10% for 8 seconds. In that 8 second window you swinging faster which feeds into the Vigor talent. Higher poison application, higher energy recovery in that 8 second window.

It's the RNG gods that are going to give you your Eviscerates or Ruptues, you can use a 3-5 combo point Eviscerate or Rupture as long as you stick to the rule of keeping separation between slice and dice and envenom. THEY HAVE TO STAY UP.
Rotation mistakes happen, just get back in your game and start over at the beginning.

Pool your energy and don't mash buttons. You will gain more dps having patience. Don't rush the rotation but let it flow.

In the rotation the damage might seem slow at the start but as mention by someone else in this tread over 50% of you damage will be poisons .
25-27% will be auto hits
Noxious Assault 15-17%
Eviscerate 6-7%
will be slightly different due to gear differences. this is just a ball park figure I got from testing this rotation on the training dummy.

If your looking to pad your damage at the beginning of the fight, use an on use trinket you can also use Oil of Immolation I know it's only a lvl 31 item but it does an extra 250 damage over 15 seconds, instant cast and has no cool down. it's spam-able every 15 seconds and the 250 damage is for each mob in a 3 yard radius, which is a benefit to our lack luster aoe.

Dragonbreath chili has a chance to do fire damage in a cone in front of the caster doing 60 damage to each mob.

Just a couple I know of and I realize some of you are more geared than I am and probably doing end game so a lot of this stuff is for new and up coming rogues

Poisons

Assassination goes through a lot of poisons. I should explain. ( Hold on to your hat Dorothy, Kansas is going bye bye).

JMHO

(Sigh) Because of the 1.3 speed daggers, now lower that dagger speed to 1.25, .97 or .87, common sense would be you are applying poisons even faster. (ie. auto attacks and combo point builder)

We have Talents that affect poison application:
Improved Poisons Increases the chance to apply poisons by 10%
Envenom Improves the chance to apply poisons to you target by 30%
Noxious Assault Strike with both weapons and applies poisons from both weapons
Slice and Dice Faster you swing the faster you chew through your poisons

now let's look at synergy between 2 other talents

Vigor Each time you poison your target you have a 100% chance to add 2 energy
Seal Fate Critical strikes from abilities that add combo points have a 100% chance to add an additional combo point.
The faster the Dagger, the higher the chance of poison application = the faster the return of energy returned to you.
That faster return of energy will be funneled into Noxious Assault Which in turn causes 2 poison stacks to disappear and gives you 1-2 combo points.
Combo points are collected to use 85% of the time on these 2 Finishers. Both feed into poison depletion
Slice and Dice
Envenom

It is a snake eating it's own tail. It's diabolical
The whole circular process is just chewing through poison stacks

but Shananagas? Isn't there something to help assassination rogue negate poison depletion?
There is a talent:
Efficient Poisons: Gives your poison application a 45% chance not to consume a charge. (A CHANCE!)
I must be the most unluckiest rogue on the planet!

With poisons falling off so fast
Assassination rogues that go OOP (out of Poisons) are just knee high gnomes tickling the boss's ankle with a feather


What I submitted due to the poison problem.

I agree
I'm an assassination rogue and the depletion of poisons is way to fast.

Efficient Poison talent is only a 45% Chance not to consume a charge. (A Chance?)

using 1.3 daggers and you throw in slice and dice and if you are wearing the Stormshroud Armor
and the 4 set procs my dagger speed is .87

I have had to revert to keeping an extra set of daggers in my bags and making a weapon swap macro
so that during trash or boss fights I can switch out because of the randomness of the 45% chance not to
consume poison charges.
Not to mention now having to double up poison purchases and loosing 2 more bag spaces.

How would I fix it?

I would just switch the talents Noxious Assault and Envenom
making Envenom the cap stone talent.

Envenom would then increase the effectiveness and chance to apply poison by 30% and also not consume your
poisons but make them 1 hour duration.

Then change Efficient Poison talent: by just taking out the bit of consuming a poison charge, and keeping the reduced chance to resist.

Envenom is a finishing move, why it's not the cap stone is beyond me.

BOOM! I have just now fixed Assassination rogue.









I am melting my enemies
I know Iknow: Daggers for life. But what do you think about using 2xFlurry Axe with this build. Bit slower but extra Attack more poison apply more Energy ticks... As a dwarf i love to crush enemy backbones with axes...
LET'S GET READY TO RUMBLE!

So you wanna talk Axes? (Hock, Spit) Don't get me wrong, Flurry Axe is a very nice level 42 weapon that is most prized by Protection Paladins

Flurry Axe
Equiped level of 42
1. A one hand Axe
2. 1.50 speed (nice)
3. DPS 35.3
4. damage range of 37-69
5 Chance on hit: Grants 1 extra attack on your next swing
Oh and it's PURPLE! Oh, How the monkeys have been train to luv the color purple. lol I admit I am a butt scratching monkey too. :)

For a level 42 it's awesome. I don't have the deep pockets to buy 2 of them but someone might and the question is at what point will you replace them with daggers. :) (Because you're going to )

Let's talk weapon skill and chance for an extra attack on your next swing.

Weapon skill: The weapon skill is capped at 315
The higher the skill the more you push misses and glancing blows off the hit table, in effect landing more attacks
which means more poison procs that turns into energy return.
Also less glancing blows = more hits that have a chance to be crits and those crits can turn into more combo points.

(A CHANCE) on hit to get an extra attack:
The Flurry Axe has a 1.5 - 2% chance to proc an extra attack, now some have said they FEEL like the proc chance is closer to 4-5% IDK but imho there is nowhere that states the extra attack proc will land 100% of the time, so the extra attack does have a chance to MISS.

You can get weapon skill for Axes, it's just so much easier to get for Daggers.

for Axes you can get Goldminers Helmet A level 33 Helm with Agi and Stam +7 to Axes ( Damn good for a level 33)
I also mentioned in a prior post of a book quest Speedz1337 (that's not easy and long) that will give +5 to axes
and there could be more gear out there for + axes that I'm not aware of.
As your gear progresses and ( I don't know what level you are) as you level, fast Daggers will just out preform axes, swords and maces (Hock,Spit)

Alcor's Sunrazor vs. Flurry Axe Main hand.
Distracting Dagger vs. Flurry Axe Off hand

It's to bad that Dwarves don't have an Axe racial like Humans have for Swords and Maces.
Duel wielding axes would be cool to see on a dwarf

Bottom line (jmho)

If you're level 42 and gots a boat load of gold (Hey Daddy, I'll be your Femboy) to buy 2 Flurry Axes Go for it, but by the time you get to your mid level 50's you will most likely be wanting to replace them IF you are planning on end content raiding.

I searched the Axe Data Base and it is the fastest axe in game and axes get slower quickly as the level goes up.

as I write this (10-13-20025) 1 Flurry axe is selling on Server Nordanaar for 400g, to duel wield, 800g
At this time only 1 is for sale

with just 400g you can buy the entire Stromshoud Armor Set (Highly recommend)

Choose your own path and have fun, at the end of the day that's what it's all about.

and if you're running Molten Core get this:

or (My Choice) x2

[Alcor's Sunrazor](https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=14555%5B/url) - World Drop, not unique so can equip 2 and it comes with +10 fire resist - +20 fire resist equiping 2 and has a nice on hit chance of fire damage (wont help in Molten Core since mobs are immune to fire damage) Outside MC    turtle_in_love_head  - Just Luv

I understand, since 2004, the rogue community has been bombarded by the Combat rogue mentality. Slower, Hard Hitting Weapons and it is hard to get out of that mindset. we see these beautiful Purple, slow Daggers drop and we drool. That's because we are trained monkeys since the beginning to want that. (lol)

The higher the skill the more you push misses and glancing blows off the hit table, in effect landing more attacks
which means more poison procs that turns into energy return.
Also less glancing blows = more hits that have a chance to be crits and those crits can turn into more combo points.

Just my Humble 2 cents: Speed of Daggers, + to Daggers, Critical Strike

Gearing: (IMHO) 4 piece [Darkmantle Armor](https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?itemset=512%5B/url) and 4 piece [Stormshroud Armor](https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?itemset=142%5B/url) : very hard for any set to beat 2x energy procs from mixing these two sets together.(jmho)
after that both [Bonescythe Armor](https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?itemset=524%5B/url) and [Trickster Armor](https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?itemset=698%5B/url) would be what I would shoot for,  [Trickster Armor](https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?itemset=698%5B/url) being my preferred armor choice.

I have all respect for combat daggers, and If you are able to get some pretty purple slow daggers, try it out.
It's those silly rogue combat warrior wanna Be's waving there sticks around that irk my nerves.   angry_turtle_hea

This has all been just my thoughts so take it with a grain of salt

content_md:
Alrighty then,
Regardless if it's retail, or private sever I have always lvled up to 56-58 ambushing and backstabbing, at times when soloing in open world I always kept sinister strike on my action bar and while in dungeons, going ham with ambushes and backstabs. In the early stages just ambush alone would drop a mobs health by 50% and who doesn't like big numbers.
If I were to say what talents to get:

lvl 10-11: Remorseless Attack, (after killing a mob, 40% increase in crit to ambush, backstab or sinister strike) lasts 40 seconds. Huge!
lvl 12-16 Camouflage ( get back in stealth in 5 seconds and increased movement speed while in stealth, Huge!
lvl 17-19 Improved Ambush ( 45% increase to crit for your ambush) Huge!
lvl 20-24 Opportunity ( Increases the crit damage to ambush and backstab by 20%) Huge!
lvl 25-27 Improved Backstab ( 30% to crit on backstab, plus 45% chance of getting a combo point) Huge!

<https://talents.turtlecraft.gg/rogue?points=C-FAD-FAY>

Your cool down on stealth is 5 sec. You lickity spit to your target and ambush (45% chance to crit) you sinister strike 3-4 times and it dies. You hit stealth and again lickity split to you next target but this time you have the remorseless attack buff which adds 40% crit to your already 45% ambush crit buff.   turtle_in_love_head   Muhahaha! And let's not forget the 20% increase to damage to your ambush from the talent Opportunity.

 1.18.0 - Rogues got a 7% increase to there run speed (A Skill learned at level 30). Which make you 7% faster in stealth. If you can get a pair of boots and put Minor Speed Enchant (gives you 8% increase speed) which makes you 15% faster now ( Holy Smolly!) compared to the last release.

Translation : "Now my question is, if you play primarily solo, but visit a dungeon every so often to gear up, is it worth staying in combat even if you don't have as much group DPS? Or is there a valid talent option for soloing and grouping while leveling?"

If your primarily is solo, play what ever spec you want and have fun, at the end of the day that is what a game is suppose to be all about.

Combat rogue has always brought good dps to group content and with some utility to boot.
gouge and blind casters, distracts and expose armor if one wants to use it.

 1.18 patch: Blade Flurry is now baseline for all specs, which brings AOE to assassination and sub.

While lvling you can run any spec you want and be able to perform well in dungeons, it's not until you are reaching level 38-39 to focus on a certain talent spec. At this point you will be able to fill out a whole talent tree and get the most out of the spec.

I ran a Ambush, Backstab build until lvl 56-58 and had a blast doing it and always did great dps in group and was having a great time in solo play.

With 1.18 I switched over to Assassination and I am loving it.

I wish I knew what level you are now and what spec you are playing to better address your answer

subject: Re: 1.18.0 - Rogue Leveling Specs
content_md:
Dagger Rogue for Life

A couple things that might help leveling.
caster
Have you ran into a situation, maybe a group dungeon or solo and you are fighting one caster but all the casters in the area look like they are casting? It happened to me in dungeons. I didn't know who to kick or gouge, it was so frustrating that I felt like I was letting the group down.
[Super Wow](https://github.com/balakethelock/SuperWoW?tab=readme-ov-file%5B/url) is a mod that fixes that mess. Now you will see only those caster that are casting.
Here is the installation guide [Super Wow Installation](https://github.com/pepopo978/SuperwowInstallation%5B/url)

Do you find yourself not knowing if you are going to pull agro off your tank, did you install a threat addon but can't find the time to look at it because of all the sweet, sweet action going on in the dungeon and all your backstab crits lighting up you screen? (sigh, I luv rogues)
[Tank Plates](https://github.com/MarcelineVQ/TankPlates%5B/url) must have [Super Wow](https://github.com/balakethelock/SuperWoW?tab=readme-ov-file%5B/url) installed as a mod.

[Tank Plates](https://github.com/MarcelineVQ/TankPlates%5B/url)

simply put it changes the color of the enemies nameplate.

Red - You don't have agro, keep on pumping you pumper.

Yellow - you need to ease up there ninja maybe use a [Feint](https://www.wowhead.com/classic/spell=1966/feint%5B/url) or chat with the pretty priest, who knows, it actually might be a woman this time.

Green - OMG! Now you done it, you couldn't hold back and you pulled, it is time to [Vanish](https://www.wowhead.com/classic/spell=1856/vanish%5B/url). Oh No! What you say? [Vanish](https://www.wowhead.com/classic/spell=1856/vanish%5B/url) is on cool down? Hit [Sprint](https://www.wowhead.com/classic/spell=2983/sprint%5B/url) little fella and scream like a little girl as your running for the portal at the beginning of the Dungeon. ( I have never done that, no really don't know what you talking about (cough)

Blue - The enemy is under CC (Kidney Shot, Blind or someone else's CC like Poly-morph) For all that's holy, don't break the CC.

I luv this addon, it's in my face with the enemy nameplates and not tucked away in the corner of my screen or in the middle of my screen blocking all my wonderful yellow crit numbers.

Also a must if you have a Tank or alt Tank.

[Trinket menu](https://github.com/S4V4GENZ/TrinketMenu%5B/url)

I'm a collector, ok maybe a hoarder. a trinket hoarder. I got alot of trinkets.

What's great about this addon is, it puts your 2 trinkets on your screen. You can mouse over and if you have another trinket in your bags it will, with just a click change your trinket (out of combat).

I have 3 trinkets ( I really have a whole lot more but let's stick to 3)

 1. is a straight forward attack power trinket, no on use effect

 2. is a straight forward agility trinket, no on use effect

 3. is a poison cloud trinket which does 50 damage every 5 sec for 45 sec with a 10 min cool down.

I join a group for a dungeon and of course the agility trinket is my bread and butter
the second trinket will be my longest cool down trinket - the poison cloud

on my screen it will show those 2 trinkets

when the tank pulls alot of mobs I can pop my poison cloud (aoe damage! Yes Plz!). the beauty of this addon is I can be in combat and mouse over the trinket I used and select another trinket.
as soon as I am out of combat it will equip that trinket I selected, which would be the attack power trinket.

Because I love chaos, mayhem and killing I use Vanish offensively and what happens when you vanish   turtle_in_love_head  it takes you out of combat so now my ambush that I'm getting ready to lay down the lord's vengeance on this mob or player (pvp) is now going to get it's damage boosted because the addon switched out trinkets as soon as I vanish (I luv being a rogue)
As soon as the poison cloud trinket is off cool down I can switch it back with just a click and use it again,(after the 30 second internal cool down) then switch back to the attack power trinket.
with a 10 min cool down you can easily use it a couple times. It's aoe damage

I do have to mention if you select an on use trinket, there is a 30 sec cool down period before you can use that trinket.
Alot of neat things you can do with your trinkets and this addon.

Easy Poison <https://github.com/Cinecom/EasyPoisons/tree/main> simplifieses the process of buying poisons.

EZ Poisons <https://github.com/wierdthing/EzPoison/tree/main> Places a button on your mini map which you left click to apply poison to your main hand and right click to apply poison to your off hand.

[Turtle WoW addon Page](https://turtle-wow.fandom.com/wiki/Addons%5B/url) You can browse at your leisure.
(I got like a gazillion addons)

Make a Macro:

Auto Attack:
This is an auto attack code that goes before any /cast skills except for ambush and gouge
If you are out of energy and need to switch targets, this will allow you to auto attack your new target Code: Select all

```
/run for i=1,120 do if IsCurrentAction(i) then return end end CastSpellByName("Attack")
```

Auto Attack with Backstab:
With the auto attack code (from up above) and Backstab, it would look like this: Code: Select all

```
/run for i=1,120 do if IsCurrentAction(i) then return end end CastSpellByName("Attack")
/cast Backstab
```

Using your trinket and casting feint, causing you to do more damage while lowering your agro
Your upper trinket slot is 13
Your lower trinket slot is 14 Code: Select all

```
/use 13
/cast Feint
```

If your trinket is on cool down or you have switched to a static trinket because you got the above [Trinket menu](https://github.com/S4V4GENZ/TrinketMenu%5B/url) Addon (Good Rogue) This macro will just cast Feint.
You have to press this macro twice to use both the  trinket and the Feint.

Mouse over Blind:

Dagger Rogue for Life

A couple things that might help leveling.
caster
Have you ran into a situation, maybe a group dungeon or solo and you are fighting one caster but all the casters in the area look like they are casting? It happened to me in dungeons. I didn't know who to kick or gouge, it was so frustrating that I felt like I was letting the group down.
Super Wow is a mod that fixes that mess. Now you will see only those caster that are casting.
Here is the installation guide Super Wow Installation

Do you find yourself not knowing if you are going to pull agro off your tank, did you install a threat addon but can't find the time to look at it because of all the sweet, sweet action going on in the dungeon and all your backstab crits lighting up you screen? (sigh, I luv rogues)
Tank Plates must have Super Wow installed as a mod.

Tank Plates

simply put it changes the color of the enemies nameplate.

Red - You don't have agro, keep on pumping you pumper.

Yellow - you need to ease up there ninja maybe use a Feint or chat with the pretty priest, who knows, it actually might be a woman this time.

Green - OMG! Now you done it, you couldn't hold back and you pulled, it is time to Vanish. Oh No! What you say? Vanish is on cool down? Hit Sprint little fella and scream like a little girl as your running for the portal at the beginning of the Dungeon. ( I have never done that, no really don't know what you talking about (cough)

Blue - The enemy is under CC (Kidney Shot, Blind or someone else's CC like Poly-morph) For all that's holy, don't break the CC.

I luv this addon, it's in my face with the enemy nameplates and not tucked away in the corner of my screen or in the middle of my screen blocking all my wonderful yellow crit numbers.

Also a must if you have a Tank or alt Tank.

Trinket menu

I'm a collector, ok maybe a hoarder. a trinket hoarder. I got alot of trinkets.

What's great about this addon is, it puts your 2 trinkets on your screen. You can mouse over and if you have another trinket in your bags it will, with just a click change your trinket (out of combat).

I have 3 trinkets ( I really have a whole lot more but let's stick to 3)

1. is a straight forward attack power trinket, no on use effect

2. is a straight forward agility trinket, no on use effect

3. is a poison cloud trinket which does 50 damage every 5 sec for 45 sec with a 10 min cool down.

I join a group for a dungeon and of course the agility trinket is my bread and butter
the second trinket will be my longest cool down trinket - the poison cloud

on my screen it will show those 2 trinkets

when the tank pulls alot of mobs I can pop my poison cloud (aoe damage! Yes Plz!). the beauty of this addon is I can be in combat and mouse over the trinket I used and select another trinket.
as soon as I am out of combat it will equip that trinket I selected, which would be the attack power trinket.

Because I love chaos, mayhem and killing I use Vanish offensively and what happens when you vanish it takes you out of combat so now my ambush that I'm getting ready to lay down the lord's vengeance on this mob or player (pvp) is now going to get it's damage boosted because the addon switched out trinkets as soon as I vanish (I luv being a rogue)

with a 10 min cool down you can easily use it a couple times. It's aoe damage

I do have to mention if you select an on use trinket, there is a 30 sec cool down period before you can use that trinket.

subject: Re: 1.18.0 - Rogue Leveling Specs
content_md:
> **Gaz wrote: Tue Sep 09, 2025 12:11 am**
> I've wanted to try playing a Subtlety Rogue for the support group aspect in dungeons. I've never played a Rogue before but was wondering what talents to go for that build. I was thinking just going deep all points in Sub and call it a day?

 1st: I have never played a turtle sub rogue before. Retail and turtle sub are total different animals. I am a crit whore and I am proud to say it ( I LUV CRIT!)

 2: Might want to rethink going all points into sub, Precision in the combat tree is just to good to pass up.

 3: As far as the build would look (see number 1)  But if I was to try a sub rogue and this is by no means based on me having any exp with playing a support rogue here on Turtle wow.

[https://talents.turtlecraft.gg/rogue?po ... YZJQAJKQoB](https://talents.turtlecraft.gg/rogue?points=Ao-FAAo-FTCYZJQAJKQoB)

Precision and Malice (IMHO) are got to haves (5% hit, 5% crit, right up my blood thirsty alley) .

Improved Exposed armor is an individual call. If your playing with a warrior then he will be putting up sunder armor and Exposed armor wont be needed, making those 2 points in Improved Exposed Armor wasted, But no warrior then you want it (maybe or maybe not, your call).

I chose Opportunity because it feeds into the Serrated Blades garrote damage, which is magnified by the lower Vanish cool down with Elusiveness which works with Cloaked in Shadows giving party members a damage bubble.

This is what I would consider more of a dungeon build.

Questing: Dropping Improved Exposed Armor and pick up Blackjack and Blinding Haze. (IMHO)

Take the above with a grain of salt.

There are sub rogues out there (I'm guessing, never met one personally) that would have way more insight than I.

If you do try any sub build please return and comment on your experiences.

 1: what level are you?

 2: I don't think anyone has done the math on Blade Rush yet. (Best Guess)
No one really knows the Devs math yet that I'm aware of but this makes the most sense to me.
 1 agility = 1 ms

anything lower 1 agility = 1ms, IMHO not sure if it would be worth getting

Blade Rush: Increases your melee attack speed by [2/5]% and reduces the time between energy regeneration ticks
by the amount equal to your agility. More effective than Blade Rush one.

A rogues energy regeneration (Baseline) is 20 energy every 2 seconds so, going from 0 energy to 100 energy will take 10 seconds. (baseline no buffs)

Blade rush as it states lowers the time of those ticks equal to the amount of agility.

(If I read this correctly):

A rogue with 500 agility will lower the time between energy ticks by .5 seconds or (half a second).
Allowing the rogue to gain 20 energy every 1.5 seconds.

A rogue with 1000 agility will lower the time between energy ticks by a full second
Allowing the rogue to gain double the amount of energy within the same time period as the baseline amount.

Putting 2 points into Blade Rush only affects the attack speed element of the talent and not the energy tick regeneration.

At a certain point there will be diminishing returns, there is only so much agility you can pile on and ( for combat Daggers) Going over crit cap has to be monitored more closely than combat (unless your are running close to BIS gear)

There will be at times, adding attack power will be more beneficial than agility based on gear level.

IMHO (in my humble opinion) It's a must have talent for combat, regardless if you go swords, maces or daggers.( Out side of the Talent Adrenaline Rush ) it's the only way (not including gear) to get more energy regeneration back which = a smoother rotation which = more damage.

I came to my thinking of 1 agility = 1ms by looking at the energy talents of the other 2 specs

Assassination: Vigor - Increases the maximum energy by [5/10]
Each time you apply poison to your target, you have a [50/100]% chance to gain 2 energy.

Subtlety: Honor among thieves - Physical critical strikes by you or party members with in 20 yards
grant you [2/5] energy.

Plain text and easy to understand, so when I read:

Combat: Blade Rush - Increases your melee attack speed by [2/5]% and
Reduces the time between your energy regeneration ticks by the amount equal to your agility
more effective than Blade Rush (Rank 1)

I think if the Devs really wanted to say:
Reduces the time between your energy regeneration ticks by the amount equal to [.75 ms] to your agility or [.50ms] to your agility, or even as low as [.25ms] to your agility. I think they would have stated that, much like the talents from the 2 other classes. JMHO

Ok, veo que voy a tener que buscar unas dagas.

lvl 28-32 Malice (Increase your crit chance by 5%) Yes please!

or

lvl 33-37 Malice (Increase your crit chance by 5%) Yes please!
lvl 38-40 Ruthlessness (Adds 100% combo point to your finishing moves on your target)

so here we go

You just dinged (gratz) and hit level 45. You now have enough points (if you so wish to) Respec and fill out a whole talent page, becoming full assassination, full combat, full sub.
OR:
lvl45-47 Improved poisons: increase the chance to apply poisons by 10%
lvl 48: Envenom: Increases the chance to apply poisons by 30%

MuHahahaha!
