[Blackstone Ring](https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=17713%5B/url) Ring - 1% hit form Princess Theradras in maraudon
[Tarnished Elven ring](https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=18500%5B/url) Ring - 1% hit from Mizzle the Crafty in Drie Maul
[Stromshroud Armor Set](https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?itemset=142%5B/url) Crafted: Gives 2% hit

and these a just a few items.

of course at any time you can during your leveling if you feel like you are missing to much you can always weave Precision in like around lvl 49. (example)

 1 point into Efficient Poisons at lvl 49,

 1 point into Precision at 54

IMHO: Change your spec at level 58, this gives you 2 levels of practice with the new build

In case you missed it and want to plot out your [Dagger Progression](https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?items=2.15%5B/url)

To All:

Pro's and Con's?

In my entire life I have never heard lamentations, but you know what? I think I want to hear them. ( not necessarily from women, unless it's lamentations of joy) lol
You know what I'm saying ladies,   satisfied_turtle_head

content_md:
Was asked about my thoughts on Life Steal enchant vs Agility enchant

Grain of salt, my 2 cents

Lifesteal is a simple enchant: get resisted or not, deal 30 dmg, heal 30 hp and create a 60 health difference.
 1. (can be resisted)
 2. Off hand has a higher miss rate than main hand (off hand has lower proc chance)
 3. Does not scale as you level, does NOT scale with any buffs
 4. There are no talents that benefit from this enchant

Agility enchant another simple enchant: 15 Agility= .5% crit, 15 attack power, adds armor and dodge.
 1. Can't be resisted
 2. Does not rely on off hand hit rating
 3. Does not scale with level but DOES scale with buffs
 4. Seal fate talent does benefit from having agility

Both enchants look like that cost about the same depending on server

At level 39, you are going to be switching up weapons a bit before hitting 60. The cheapest enchant (unless you got deep pockets) would be [Fiery Weapon](https://www.wowhead.com/classic/spell=13898/enchant-weapon-fiery-weapon%5B/url)
Which does 40 damage but no heal

I'm a crit whore so you know which enchant I like
It's all up to you   satisfied_turtle_head

author: Idontcareatall
subject: Re: Rogue  Leveling?
content_md:
Yeah, that's because the monsters on this servers were buffed to make up for all the buffs the other classes received, mainly Paladin the golden child of the TWoW team.

Unfortunately, even though Rogues also received some buffs/QoL, it's nowhere near enough to make up for it during the leveling process. You're basically a leather wearer with no healing abilities, fighting against beefed up monsters.

I'd argue Rogue is the worst solo class atm. Don't get me wrong, Warriors are still trash also, but they received many QoL, and you can easily go into dungeons to tank and access great items.

As a rogue, not only are you weak in the outside world, you also can't instant tag a dungeon the way a warrior can. And you're also undesirable: you bring nothing to the party, and you'll also be frequently kicked by warriors that don't want you to compete on their weapons, and druid tanks that don't want you to compete on their leather.

I'm leveling my rogue (level 49 atm) by dual-boxing it with a Shaman, which gives me the heals and WF buff to slice monsters, but otherwise I would not bother.

Of course, I go with this build: [https://talents.turtlecraft.gg/rogue?po ... FADo-FDYYY](https://talents.turtlecraft.gg/rogue?points=CoCBAo-FADo-FDYYY)

Lv 10-19
 2 points in Camofaluge
 3 points in Improved Gouge
 3 points in Improved Ambush
 2 points in Remorseless Attacks

Lv 20-29
 5 points in Opportunity
 3 points in Improved Backstab
 2 points in Camofaluge

Lv 30-35
 1 point in Camofaluge
 5 points in Precision

From here on out you can experiment with other talents. I recommend specting into things that further boost your Ambush so it will consistently slash away huge chunks of the enemy's HP. Your rotation is very straighforward: Ambush -> Gauge -> Backstab -> Eviscerate. If the target is not dead, use Sinister Strike or repeat the Gauge -> Backstab rotation.

author: Tankmeister
subject: The many issues with Subtlety
content_md:
This is mainly from a PvP perspective. I find that several deep sub talents are very lackluster and/or totally messed up in their current state...

 - Smoke Bomb -
I was excited to try this one out. I like the idea of the sub rogue being elusive and harder to hit, which fits the archetype imo. However, I just cannot make good use of this ability. I think the problem stems from the fact that it affects ALL within the area, not just allies. Furthermore, it has a FIVE MINUTE cooldown!? It's extremely situational at best.

 - Cloaked in Shadows -
Make the absorption shield not break stealth when absorbing damage - that would fix this talent. Right now, the shield for you and allies isn't terrible, but it isn't something you're gonna pop vanish for.

 - Blinding Haze -
It lasts only for 6 seconds and reduces hit change by 6%... I dunno, I think this one just sucks. This just needs a numbers tweak to make it good.

 - Shadow of Death -
This one is just a mess in my opinion. You're supposed to spend all your combo points on an ability that requires you to do damage in the next 6 seconds? This shouldn't be a finishing move - it makes absolutely no sense. As it stands you're heavily dependent on teammates doing the damage, and it doesn't feel right. It has the potential to do good damage but it isn't enough to justify the finicky nature of it.

 - Tricks of the Trade -
As someone else mentioned in another post - this one sucks and isn't worth spending 5 points into for anyone. Numbers are too low.

 - Mark for Death -
This really confused me when I tried it out for the first time. I totally expected it to put a debuff on an enemy (judging from the name + description and the fact that it is an attack), but it just gives everyone a buff instead. Sure, buffing everyone is more powerful but thematically it is a bit of an absurd design in my opinion. What I would like to see instead, is a move you can cast from within stealth, that puts 2 combo points and puts a strong debuff on a target. That would just make a lot more sense and would fit the playstyle better and would be more fun I think.

Overall, I think the sub tree is a bit all over the place in terms of vision. I don't mind the "support" direction, but how it is implemented now just feels awful. One problem is that you depend too much on allies (Shadow of Death, Tricks of the Trade) and that really isn't fun. I think a sub rogue can be supportive in other ways that ARE fun, and I think the team should lean more into stealth, elusiveness and CC much more. I'm imagining a rogue that is difficult to lock down, that disables the enemy, and can support the team with e.g better designed smoke bomb and mark for death.

author: Lomikare1
subject: Subtlety Rogue rework proposal
content_md:
**Greetings to all players and developers of this amazing game!**

I’ve put together a proposal for changes to the Subtlety Rogue spec that puts a stronger emphasis on stealth‑oriented gameplay. Subtlety has always been the spec most closely tied to stealth, ambushes, and powerful opening moves, and I believe it’s a shame that the current talent setup doesn’t fully reflect that fantasy.

Using a tool that allows custom talent‑tree creation, I built a reworked Subtlety talent tree. I then reached out to several experienced Rogue players, including dedicated Subtlety mains, and refined the proposal based on their feedback. The result should be fairly polished — but if you notice anything that could be improved, I’d really appreciate your feedback! O:)

 **Link to the standalone Subtlety talent tree:**
<https://talent-builder.haaxor1689.dev/tree/_Ebz_RPLVq>
 **Link to the full talent calculator including other subclasses:**
[https://talent-builder.haaxor1689.dev/c ... ImNlhSSzfP](https://talent-builder.haaxor1689.dev/calculator?t2=_Ebz_RPLVq&t1=BgHtMNM2mb&t0=ImNlhSSzfP)
 **Link to the new Subtlety tree with the old one shown side‑by‑side for comparison:**
[https://talent-builder.haaxor1689.dev/c ... 19&class=8](https://talent-builder.haaxor1689.dev/calculator?t2=_Ebz_RPLVq&t1=ATUjVOc819&class=8)

 **LIST OF INDIVIDUAL TALENT CHANGES**
 **1. ROW**
Improved gouge: the talent no longer increases the duration of Gouge, but instead reduces its Energy cost. This change was made to improve its synergy with other talents in the Subtlety.

Camuflage:  now has 3 talent points instead of 5. The effect stays mostly the same. The difference is a 1‑second reduced cooldown on stealth abilities, so overall it’s a buff. The increased movement speed in Stealth now has a much stronger impact in PvE encounters as well.

 **2. ROW**
Improved ambush:  its position was moved slightly to the right for visual clarity. The effect remains unchanged.

Blackjack: moved from the 4th row to the 2nd row, making it more accessible early while leveling and adding more diversity in PvP.

 **3. ROW**
Gouging shadows (NEW): Gouge is gaining a new effect that gives Subtlety Rogues better access to stealth and stronger opening moves. The cooldown on Gouge is intentionally increased — partly for PvP balance, and partly to make the overall rotation feel a bit less frantic.
Note: For PvP, Cheap Shot would need a small rework — specifically adding a cooldown. Having a free Cheap Shot every 20 seconds could break PvP. Ideally, Cheap Shot should share a similar cooldown to Kidney Shot.

Dirty deeds:  moved from the 5th row to the 3rd row, placing it alongside Initiative. It now has 3 ranks and reduces the cost of Garrote and Ambush (but not Cheap Shot). Cheap Shot is already strong in PvP.

Initiative: no longer grants a bonus combo point on Cheap Shot openers. As mentioned earlier, Cheap Shot is already very strong in PvP.

Smoke Bomb: removed. It was a cool idea, but far too difficult to implement properly in both PvP and PvE. If it absolutely needs to stay in some form, it should only exist as a class‑specific consumable (similar to Rogue Thistle Tea, Blinding Powder, etc.).

 **4. ROW**
Ellusivnes: moved to the 4th row and now has 3 ranks. It’s buffed: with 3 points invested, it reduces the cooldown of Blind and Vanish to a total of 90 seconds. This allows Vanish and Blind to be used twice (or three times with Preparation) per boss encounter. Elusiveness becomes even stronger thanks to Stealth Surge.

 **5. ROW**
Stealt surge (NEW): new talent that reinforces the subclass fantasy of a stealth killer and increases the importance of Vanish and Elusiveness.

 **6. ROW**
Honor Among Thieves: swapped position but remains in the same row for cosmetic reasons. It’s buffed, as it was previously the weakest energy generator. It can now also be triggered by the rogue himself.

Deadlines (NEW): It increases attack power, which is the best stat for Subtlety rogues. This is why it’s placed on the same row as Tricks of the Trade. Sub rogues now have to choose whether they want to be more supportive or focus on personal damage.

author: Lomikare1
subject: Simple Fix for Rogue Tank Threat Problems
content_md:
**Dear developers,**

I’ve been playing the unconventional Rogue tank specialization for several years now — yes, there are still players who enjoy it because of how unique it is.

Rogue tanks currently face one major issue: the poison that boosts our threat deals Poison damage, and a surprising number of enemies are immune to it. These enemies become extremely difficult, almost impossible, for us to tank. It’s comparable to Paladins suddenly losing Righteous Fury or Warriors losing their Defensive Stance threat bonus on a large portion of bosses or mobs.

The fix is simple and consistent with previous adjustments to rogue poisons: Agitating Poison should deal Physical damage instead.

 **Proposed change**
 *Agitating Poison → renamed to Itching Poison: now deals Physical damage instead of Nature damage.*

Thank you for taking the time to read this, and I wish you smooth progress in developing this wonderful game.

It has also been brought to our attention that some crafty rogues use flourish to farm some end game bosses alone or in a much smaller group than intended. For that reason, we decided to put a cd on Flourish, to make reaching avoidance cap much harder. Expect more changes for rogue tanking, and rogue class as a whole in the next round of spell changes.
It is not related directly to poisons, but shows why rogues are not going to be true tanks in turtle.
